evidence_items.explanation: The authors report progress in controlling assistant behavior while reducing human supervision. This challenges a literal claim of no alignment research progress, but does not demonstrate a general solution or establish its distance from completion.

The study finds that weaker supervisors can elicit some stronger-model capabilities, addressing a relevant supervision obstacle. Its experiments are an analogy to future superhuman alignment, and the authors acknowledge that naive methods fail to recover full capabilities.

evidence_items.publisher: International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI, published by the UK government
evidence_items.explanation: The assessment notes improved control in some recent systems while finding the direction of future controllability uncertain. It supports separating demonstrated local advances from an established trajectory toward a general solution.

unresolved_gaps: No common measure connects the documented advances to overall distance from a general alignment solution.
The sources do not provide a comparable April 2022 and June 2024 assessment of all principal alignment barriers.
Transfer from current-model experiments to dependable alignment of more capable systems remains uncertain.
